sentences.en: For this, the inaugural year, they've chosen to celebrate The Daily.

sentences.en: We know you, our incredible audience, live all over the world.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，你们——我们不可思议的听众——遍布世界各地。

sentences.en: But we'd like to invite you to join us.
sentences.zh: 但我们想邀请您加入我们。

sentences.zh: 这场盛典将于6月9日下午5点在纽约举行。

sentences.en: You can get all the details and buy tickets at tribecafilm.com slash the daily.
sentences.zh: 您可以获取所有详情并购票，网址是 tribecafilm.com 斜杠 the daily。

sentences.zh: 所以如果你在当地或者来这里参观，我们很希望能见到你。

sentences.en: Okay, on with today's show.
sentences.zh: 好了，继续今天的节目。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这里是《今日》。

sentences.en: I have got a bone to pick, as usual, with Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我对Ticketmaster（特狮买票网）有一肚子意见要发泄。

sentences.en: The biggest problem that I have right now is not getting tickets to the AeroTour.
sentences.zh: 我现在最大的问题不是买不到AeroTour巡演的门票。

sentences.en: Loading, loading, loading, when I'm so bad, when I'm so bad, when I'm so bad.
sentences.zh: 加载中，加载中，加载中，当我表现得太差，当我表现得太差，当我表现得太差。

sentences.en: Oh, nope.
sentences.zh: 哦，没有。

sentences.en: I looked at my account and the tickets are gone.
sentences.zh: 我查了我的账号，票已经没了。

sentences.en: Over the past few years, few companies have provoked as much anger.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，很少有公司能引发这么大的愤怒。

sentences.en: I cannot afford $1,500 tickets.
sentences.zh: 我买不起1500美元的门票。

sentences.en: Among music fans.
sentences.zh: 在音乐粉丝中间。

sentences.en: Oh my God!
sentences.zh: 我的天哪！

sentences.en: As Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 像Ticketmaster一样。

sentences.en: I literally hate Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 我简直恨死Ticketmaster了。

sentences.en: Like, there is no company I think I hate more than Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 就好像，我觉得没有任何一家公司比Ticketmaster更让我讨厌了。

sentences.en: Ticketmaster ought to look in the mirror and say, I'm the problem.
sentences.zh: Ticketmaster应该照照镜子，说：我就是问题所在。

sentences.en: It's me.
sentences.zh: 就是我。

sentences.en: Last week, the Department of Justice announced it was taking the company to court.
sentences.zh: 上周，司法部宣布将该公司告上法庭。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, David McCabe, on how the government's case could reshape America's multi-billion dollar live music industry.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·麦凯布将探讨政府的诉讼将如何重塑美国价值数十亿美元的现场音乐产业。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, May 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月30日，星期四。

sentences.en: So, David, good to have you back.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，欢迎你回来。

sentences.en: You have become a beloved guest at The Daily because the government keeps bringing these huge antitrust cases and we keep turning to you to explain them.
sentences.zh: 你已经成了《今日》节目的受欢迎嘉宾，因为政府一直在提起这些重大的反垄断诉讼，而我们总是找你来解释它们。

sentences.en: Well, it's a pleasure to be back.
sentences.zh: 很高兴回来。

sentences.en: And today I have a question for you, which is, what was the first concert you ever went to?
sentences.zh: 今天我有一个问题要问你，那就是，你看的第一场演唱会是什么？

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, the first concert I ever went to.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，我去看的第一场演唱会。

sentences.en: Oh my God, I think it was Van Halen in the 1980s, which maybe is before you were born?
sentences.zh: 天哪，我想那是20世纪80年代的范·海伦乐队，也许这比你出生还要早？

sentences.en: You know, no comment, but that's a pretty good first concert.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无可奉告，但那确实是一场相当不错的第一场演唱会。

sentences.en: And the case that we're here to talk about today is actually all about shows like a Van
sentences.zh: 我们今天要谈论的这个案子，其实就跟1980年代范·海伦演唱会

sentences.en: Halen concert in 1980.
sentences.zh: 这样的演出息息相关。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm ready.
sentences.zh: 好的，我准备好了。

sentences.en: So let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 那我们开始吧。

sentences.en: This case, as you and I both know, is about Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 如你我所知，这个案子是关于Ticketmaster的。

sentences.en: So tell us about this case.
sentences.zh: 那么给我们讲讲这个案子吧。

sentences.en: So anyone who attends concerts regularly or even irregularly probably knows about Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 任何经常或甚至偶尔去看演唱会的人大概都知道Ticketmaster。

sentences.en: It's kind of the ubiquitous digital box office.
sentences.zh: 它有点像无处不在的数字售票处。

sentences.en: And those people are probably also familiar with the ubiquitous fan complaints about Ticketmaster,
sentences.zh: 这些人可能也对关于Ticketmaster的种种普遍抱怨司空见惯，

sentences.en: that the company puts high fees that they don't entirely explain onto tickets, that tickets will sell out really fast during these sort of frantic pre-sales for tours, and that the
sentences.zh: 比如该公司在门票上附加了他们没有完全解释清楚的高额费用，门票在巡演那种疯狂的预售期间会卖得极快，而且

sentences.en: website doesn't always work very well.
sentences.zh: 网站运作得并不总是那么好。

sentences.en: And probably the most infamous Ticketmaster incident in recent memory was a couple years ago when the pre-sale began for Taylor Swift's massive Iris tour.
sentences.zh: 近来最臭名昭著的Ticketmaster事件大概是几年前泰勒·斯威夫特盛大的“时代巡回演唱会”开始预售的时候。

sentences.en: And fans got locked out, couldn't get tickets, and were absolutely furious.
sentences.zh: 粉丝们被拒之门外，买不到票，愤怒至极。

sentences.en: And it really put in the spotlight the power of this company over the ability to buy a ticket to a live music event.
sentences.zh: 这确实让这家公司对购买现场音乐活动门票的掌控力成为了焦点。

sentences.en: So the DOJ is pointing the finger at this company for all this consumer angst, at Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 因此，司法部将所有这些消费者怨气的矛头指向了这家公司，指向了Ticketmaster。

sentences.en: Well, and when you say this company, it's not just Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你提到这家公司时，不只是Ticketmaster。

sentences.en: It's the company that owns Ticketmaster, a company called Live Nation Entertainment.
sentences.zh: 它是拥有Ticketmaster的公司，一家名为“直播国度娱乐”的公司。

sentences.en: We'll say Live Nation for short.
sentences.zh: 我们简称它为“直播国度”。

sentences.en: And it's a giant company.
sentences.zh: 这是一 家巨型公司。

sentences.en: And to think about just how gigantic and how expansive Live Nation is, I think it's helpful to think about the fan experience of going to a concert.
sentences.zh: 要理解“直播国度”到底有多庞大、多广泛，我认为回顾一下去看演唱会的粉丝体验会很有帮助。

sentences.en: It starts with buying a ticket.
sentences.zh: 它从买票开始。

sentences.en: And maybe you buy a group of tickets for you and your friends.
sentences.zh: 也许你为自己和朋友买了一组票。

sentences.en: And then one of your friends can't make it.
sentences.zh: 然后你的一个朋友去不了了。

sentences.en: They got other plans.
sentences.zh: 他们有别的安排。

sentences.en: You resell their ticket so you can make your money back.
sentences.zh: 你转售他们的票，这样就能把钱赚回来。

sentences.en: And then the day of the show, you go.
sentences.zh: 演出当天，你去了。

sentences.en: It's this big production.
sentences.zh: 这是一场盛大的制作。

sentences.en: It's at a venue.
sentences.zh: 它在某个场馆举行。

sentences.en: Someone has booked the artist to appear.
sentences.zh: 有人预订了这位艺术家来演出。

sentences.en: You go.
sentences.zh: 你去了。

sentences.en: You buy a beer.
sentences.zh: 你买了一杯啤酒。

sentences.en: You have a good time.
sentences.zh: 你玩得很开心。

sentences.en: Live Nation is involved in many parts of that process.
sentences.zh: “直播国度”参与了这一过程的许多环节。

sentences.en: And that starts with being a major concert promoter.
sentences.zh: 首先它是一家大型演唱会主办方。

sentences.en: They're the one putting it on, arranging the event.
sentences.zh: 他们是举办活动、安排演出的人。

sentences.en: They're also selling the tickets through Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 他们还通过Ticketmaster售票。

sentences.en: Sometimes they're also involved in reselling the tickets when your friend can't make it.
sentences.zh: 有时，当你的朋友去不了时，他们也会参与门票的转售。

sentences.en: And not only that, they actually sometimes manage the artists and they own or operate the venues where the show is happening.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们实际上有时还管理艺术家，并且拥有或运营演出发生的场馆。

sentences.en: So even down to that beer you're drinking to enjoy it with the show, they might be involved in picking the person who sells that beer to you.
sentences.zh: 所以甚至连你为了享受演出而喝的那杯啤酒，他们都可能参与挑选向你出售啤酒的人。

sentences.en: So basically, they're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们无处不在。

sentences.en: They're everywhere.
sentences.zh: 无处不在。

sentences.en: And the Justice Department says that's a big part of the problem, that its power is bad for fans.
sentences.zh: 司法部表示，这正是问题的很大一部分所在，其权力对粉丝有害。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Earlier today, the Department of Justice...
sentences.zh: 今天早些时候，司法部……

sentences.en: And we really heard that come through at the press conference last week that the Justice
sentences.zh: 我们在上周司法部为宣布此案而举行的

sentences.en: Department held to announce this case.
sentences.zh: 新闻发布会上确实听到了这一点。

sentences.en: People always remember the first time that they were transformed by live music.
sentences.zh: 人们总是记得他们第一次被现场音乐震撼的经历。

sentences.en: Where Merrick Garland, the Attorney General, really personalized this issue.
sentences.zh: 司法部长梅里克·加兰真正将这个问题个人化了。

sentences.en: I still remember, as a senior in college, going to a Bonnie Raitt concert and seeing a...
sentences.zh: 我还记得，作为大学高年级学生，去看邦妮·雷特的一场演唱会，看到一个……

sentences.en: He told this story about going to a Bonnie Raitt concert in college.
sentences.zh: 他讲述了自己在大学时去看邦妮·雷特演唱会的故事。

sentences.en: Merrick Garland did?
sentences.zh: 梅里克·加兰讲的？

sentences.en: Yeah, Merrick Garland did.
sentences.zh: 对，梅里克·加兰讲的。

sentences.en: I don't think of Merrick Garland and Bonnie Raitt together in the same sentence.
sentences.zh: 我不会把梅里克·加兰和邦妮·雷特联系在同一句话里。

sentences.en: Well, apparently in college, he attended a Bonnie Raitt show.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然他在大学时去看过邦妮·雷特的演出。

sentences.en: And the thing he highlighted was that the opener was a young Bruce Springsteen.
sentences.zh: 他强调的是，暖场嘉宾是一个年轻的布鲁斯·斯普林斯廷。

sentences.en: We all know that we had just seen the future of rock and roll.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道我们刚刚看到了摇滚乐的未来。

sentences.en: And in that story, the Attorney General seems to be getting at two important threads of this case.
sentences.zh: 在这个故事中，司法部长似乎在探讨这个案件的两个重要线索。

sentences.en: The first is that concerts are formative for the people who attend them.
sentences.zh: 首先，演唱会对参加的人来说具有塑造性意义。

sentences.en: And the second is that concerts are an important way that artists reach their fans.
sentences.zh: 其次，演唱会是艺术家接触粉丝的重要途径。

sentences.en: That young Bruce Springsteen went on to now be one of the biggest touring artists in the world.
sentences.zh: 那个年轻的布鲁斯·斯普林斯廷后来成为了世界上巡演规模最大的艺术家之一。

sentences.en: The Justice Department filed this lawsuit on behalf of fans who should be able to go to concerts without a monopoly standing in their way.
sentences.zh: 司法部代表那些本应能够去看演唱会而不受垄断阻碍的粉丝提起了这起诉讼。

sentences.en: We have filed this lawsuit on behalf of artists who should be able...
sentences.zh: 我们代表那些本应能够……的艺术家提起了这起诉讼。

sentences.en: And so the Justice Department is responding here to a feeling that Live Nation, this giant company, has become a gatekeeper for both artists and fans.
sentences.zh: 因此，司法部在这里做出的回应是，人们普遍感觉到像“直播国度”这样的大公司已经成了艺术家和粉丝的守门人。

sentences.en: And that has allowed it to pay artists less sometimes, but also charge fans those fees that they're so mad about.
sentences.zh: 这使得它有时可以少付给艺术家报酬，但也向粉丝收取让他们如此愤怒的费用。

sentences.en: It is time for fans and artists to stop paying the price for Live Nation's monopoly.
sentences.zh: 是时候让粉丝和艺术家停止为“直播国度”的垄断付出代价了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So help us understand how things have gotten to this point, where Live Nation is so powerful that the DOJ feels the need to sue them.
sentences.zh: 那么请帮我们理解，事情怎么会发展到这一步，以至于司法部觉得有必要起诉他们？

sentences.en: Well, this company has a long history of tangling with the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这家公司与司法部纠缠的历史很长。

sentences.en: And that really starts in 2009, when Live Nation and Ticketmaster announced that they were going to merge.
sentences.zh: 这其实始于2009年，当时“直播国度”和Ticketmaster宣布他们将要合并。

sentences.en: And this merger, this big corporate deal, will marry Live Nation's concert promotion business,
sentences.zh: 这次合并，这桩大型企业交易，将“直播国度”的演唱会主办业务——

sentences.en: the business of putting on shows, with Ticketmaster's experience as an online ticketing platform.
sentences.zh: 举办演出的业务，与Ticketmaster作为在线票务平台的经验结合在了一起。

sentences.en: And the Justice Department, a big part of its job, is looking at corporate mergers to figure out if they will substantially lessen competition in the economy.
sentences.zh: 司法部的工作很大一部分是审查企业合并，以判断它们是否会大幅削弱经济中的竞争。

sentences.en: So the Justice Department reviews this merger, and in 2010 decides, we will let this merger go
sentences.zh: 因此，司法部审查了这起合并，并在2010年决定，我们允许这次合并

sentences.en: through, but we do have some concerns that it might reduce competition in the industry of ticketing.
sentences.zh: 进行，但我们确实担心它可能会降低票务行业的竞争。

sentences.en: And so we're going to reach a legal settlement with Live Nation and Ticketmaster that puts conditions on the deal, that requires the company to sell some assets to kind of lessen
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将与“直播国度”和Ticketmaster达成一项法律和解，对这笔交易施加条件，要求该公司出售部分资产以缩减

sentences.en: its footprint.
sentences.zh: 其业务规模。

sentences.en: And so the merger goes through, and that creates the sort of modern-day Live Nation-Ticketmaster combination.
sentences.zh: 于是合并得以进行，这就形成了当今的“直播国度-Ticketmaster”组合。

sentences.en: So the government ultimately actually just lets it happen.
sentences.zh: 所以政府最终实际上还是放任它发生了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They put conditions on the merger, but ultimately, they let it go through.
sentences.zh: 他们对合并施加了条件，但最终还是放行了。

sentences.en: And the company continues to tangle with the Justice Department over the next 15 or so years, but mostly they keep getting bigger.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的15年左右时间里，该公司继续与司法部纠缠，但大多数时候它们越做越大。

sentences.en: They keep growing their footprint across this ecosystem that creates some of the biggest concert tours in the country.
sentences.zh: 它们不断扩大自己在整个生态系统中的足迹，而这个生态系统缔造了国内一些最大的演唱会巡演。

sentences.en: So just how big has the company actually become?
sentences.zh: 那么这家公司到底变得有多大？

sentences.en: Give me some numbers.
sentences.zh: 给我一些数字。

sentences.en: Well, let's start here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们从这里开始。

sentences.en: Every year, they sell about 600 million tickets.
sentences.zh: 他们每年售出大约6亿张门票。

sentences.en: 600 million tickets?
sentences.zh: 6亿张门票？

sentences.en: That's more than the number of people in the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 这比美利坚合众国的人口还要多。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that is a global number, but it's a lot of tickets, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个全球数字，但这也是相当多的票，对吧？

sentences.en: The Department of Justice estimates that in the United States, Live Nation controls about
sentences.zh: 司法部估计，在美国，“直播国度”控制了大约

sentences.en: 80% of ticketing to major venue concerts.
sentences.zh: 80%的大型场馆演唱会票务。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So that's a big percentage.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个很大的比例。

sentences.en: They also own or control like in excess of 250 venues, including a big percentage, the
sentences.zh: 他们还拥有或控制着超过250个场馆，司法部表示，其中包含很大一部分的大型露天剧场，

sentences.en: Justice Department says, of major amphitheaters, the kind of big outdoor concert venues that
sentences.zh: 也就是那种介于夜总会和大型足球场规模之间的

sentences.en: are ultimately kind of in between a nightclub and the size of like a big football stadium.
sentences.zh: 大型户外演唱会场馆。

sentences.en: And they manage hundreds of artists.
sentences.zh: 而且他们管理着数百名艺术家。

sentences.en: They have this direct relationship with artists.
sentences.zh: 他们与艺术家之间有着这种直接的联系。

sentences.en: And so this company is wide and it is deep into this industry.
sentences.zh: 因此，这家公司的业务范围既广又深，深入到这个行业的方方面面。

sentences.en: So ultimately, the Justice Department says that, and I'm going to quote here, it's the quote, gatekeeper for delivery of nearly all live music in America today.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，司法部表示——我在这里引用原话，原话是——它是当今美国几乎所有现场音乐演出的分发看门人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: It's big.
sentences.zh: 这体量很大。

sentences.en: But as we know from other DOJ cases, and this is something that you have taught me, David,
sentences.zh: 但正如我们从司法部的其他案件中了解到的那样，这也是你教过我的，大卫，

sentences.en: the cases, you know, against Apple and Google, just being big is not in and of itself a problem.
sentences.zh: 那些针对苹果和谷歌的案件表明，仅仅体量大本身并不是问题。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没。错。

sentences.en: Where companies run afoul of the law is when they use their power as a monopoly against their competitors in order to stay powerful or get more powerful.
sentences.zh: 公司触犯法律的地方在于，它们利用垄断权力来对付竞争对手，从而维持权力或获取更大的权力。

sentences.en: And the Justice Department says that Live Nation has built a complex machine to do just that.
sentences.zh: 而司法部表示，Live Nation 建立了一套复杂的机器，恰恰就是为了做到这一点。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温纳露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天都创作拼字游戏《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到声音的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 键入 games 开始畅玩今天的游戏。

sentences.en: So what does the DOJ say that Live Nation is able to do because it is so big?
sentences.zh: 那么，司法部认为 Live Nation 凭借其庞大的体量能够做到什么？

sentences.en: How does it use its bigness?
sentences.zh: 它如何利用自己的体量优势？

sentences.en: So the most prominent allegation is that Live Nation uses its power as a concert promoter to entrench its power in ticketing.
sentences.zh: 最突出的指控是，Live Nation 利用其作为演唱会主办方的权力，来巩固其在票务领域的权力。

sentences.en: As a reminder, when you put together a concert, a promoter works with an artist to book the show.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，当你筹办一场演唱会时，主办方会与艺术家合作来预订演出。

sentences.en: They book the show at a venue, and that venue, for all of its shows, has to choose a ticketing provider, right?
sentences.zh: 他们在某个场馆预订演出，而该场馆的所有演出都必须选择一个票务供应商，对吧？

sentences.en: A digital box office where people can buy their way into the shows.
sentences.zh: 一个让人们可以买票入场的数字售票处。

sentences.en: And what the Justice Department is arguing here is that Live Nation is able to wield its big artists, the tours that it promotes, as a cudgel to force venues to use Ticketmaster,
sentences.zh: 司法部在这里辩称的是，Live Nation 能够利用其旗下的超级巨星和它主办的巡演作为大棒，迫使场馆使用 Ticketmaster，

sentences.en: its ticketing service.
sentences.zh: 也就是它的票务服务。

sentences.en: So the Justice Department says that in an instance in which a venue switched away from using
sentences.zh: 因此，司法部表示，在某个场馆停止使用

sentences.en: Ticketmaster, that Live Nation routed tours around that venue, which of course means less money for that venue and a problem for their business.
sentences.zh: Ticketmaster 的情况下，Live Nation 会将巡演路线绕开该场馆，这当然意味着该场馆的收入减少，并给他们的业务带来麻烦。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So basically, Live Nation saying, look, if you want Taylor Swift in your little amphitheater over there, you're going to have to use Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，Live Nation 的意思是：听着，如果你想让泰勒·斯威夫特去你那边的小露天剧场，你就必须使用 Ticketmaster。

sentences.en: It's Ticketmaster or no Taylor Swift.
sentences.zh: 要么用 Ticketmaster，要么就没有泰勒·斯威夫特。

sentences.en: That is effectively the behavior the Justice Department is arguing has happened here.
sentences.zh: 司法部认为这里发生的正是这种行为。

sentences.en: They're saying that Live Nation does this in veiled ways, and that more importantly, it's
sentences.zh: 他们表示，Live Nation 以隐蔽的方式这样做，更重要的是，

sentences.en: really understood by venues throughout the industry that if you don't use Ticketmaster, that you really risk out on losing important Live Nation-managed tours.
sentences.zh: 整个行业的场馆都心知肚明，如果你不使用 Ticketmaster，你真的会面临错失由 Live Nation 管理的重要巡演的风险。

sentences.en: And that once these venues do choose Ticketmaster, Live Nation locks them into these long, exclusive ticketing contracts, which can last for as long as 14 years.
sentences.zh: 而且一旦这些场馆选择了 Ticketmaster，Live Nation 就会把它们锁死在长期、独家的票务合同中，这些合同长达 14 年。

sentences.en: 14 years?
That's pretty long.
sentences.zh: 那可真够长的。

sentences.en: What else is DOJ alleging that Live Nation has done?
sentences.zh: 司法部还指控 Live Nation 做过什么？

sentences.en: Another thing the Justice Department says that Live Nation does is use its power as an owner of venues to get away with paying artists less money for their tours.
sentences.zh: 司法部表示 Live Nation 做的另一件事是，利用其作为场馆所有者的权力，在支付艺术家巡演报酬时少付钱。

sentences.en: So how does that work?
sentences.zh: 那这是怎么运作的呢？

sentences.en: Basically, the argument is that because Live Nation controls so many of certain types of venues, that there are instances in which an artist tour might largely be dominated by
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们的论点是，由于 Live Nation 控制了某一类型的大量场馆，在某些情况下，艺术家的巡演可能主要由

sentences.en: Live Nation-owned venues.
sentences.zh: Live Nation 拥有的场馆主导。

sentences.en: And the Justice Department is saying that Live Nation knows that artists don't have a lot
sentences.zh: 司法部表示，Live Nation 深知艺术家们在举办演唱会的地点选择上并没有太多其他选择，

sentences.en: of other options for where to play their concerts, and as a result, is able to pay those artists less because there's not competitive pressure when they're booking those tours.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于在预订这些巡演时缺乏竞争压力，他们能够向这些艺术家支付更少的报酬。

sentences.en: That seems pretty unfair to artists who would really benefit from other venues owned by other people competing for them.
sentences.zh: 对于那些如果能从其他人拥有的、为争夺他们而竞争的场馆中真正受益的艺术家来说，这似乎很不公平。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what the Justice Department is saying, that artists lose out, not just fans.
sentences.zh: 而这正是司法部所说的，受到损害的不只是歌迷，还有艺术家。

sentences.en: And there's a striking story in the complaint that I think crystallizes how the Justice Department sees these streams of power coming together.
sentences.zh: 起诉书中有一个引人注目的故事，我认为它清晰地展现了司法部如何看待这些权力流的汇聚。

sentences.en: And it concerns a concert, which the lawsuit doesn't name, in 2021.
sentences.zh: 它涉及 2021 年的一场音乐会，诉讼中未具名。

sentences.en: My colleague Ben Cesario has reported that it was a Kanye West concert featuring Drake, it was a benefit show, and it was taking place at the L.A.
sentences.zh: 我的同事本·塞萨里奥报道称，那是一场由德雷克助阵的坎耶·韦斯特演唱会，这是一场慈善演出，在洛杉矶的洛杉矶纪念体育场

sentences.en: Coliseum in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 举行。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: One of the companies involved in putting on this show was a firm called TEG.
sentences.zh: 参与筹办这场演出的公司之一是一家名为 TEG 的公司。

sentences.en: They do promotion and ticketing of the kind that Live Nation does.
sentences.zh: 他们从事 Live Nation 那样的演出推广和票务工作。

sentences.en: And the government says that Live Nation saw this as a threat, that they saw this company,
sentences.zh: 政府表示，Live Nation 将此视为一种威胁，他们看到这家公司

sentences.en: TEG, involved in this show, and they were worried about what it would mean for them.
sentences.zh: TEG 参与了这场演出，并开始担心这会对他们意味着什么。

sentences.en: And that they then undertook steps to put pressure on TEG and make their life difficult in a couple ways.
sentences.zh: 于是他们采取措施对 TEG 施加压力，在几个方面让对方的日子不好过。

sentences.en: The first was that TEG had reached a deal to sell some tickets, according to the complaint, through StubHub.
sentences.zh: 首先是根据起诉书，TEG 已经达成了一项通过 StubHub 出售部分门票的协议。

sentences.en: StubHub, it's a secondary resale market.
sentences.zh: StubHub 是一个二级门票转售市场。

sentences.en: You know, you can buy tickets to shows when people aren't going to use them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当人们不打算去的时候，你可以在那里买到演出门票。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And competitor to Ticketmaster, right?
sentences.zh: 而且是 Ticketmaster 的竞争对手，对吧？

sentences.en: And competitor to Ticketmaster.
sentences.zh: 也是 Ticketmaster 的竞争对手。

sentences.en: And the Justice Department says that Live Nation found out about that and said, well, we have the exclusive ticketing contract for this venue.
sentences.zh: 司法部表示，Live Nation 发现了这一点并表示：好吧，我们拥有该场馆的独家票务合同。

sentences.en: And so we will make sure that if you bought your ticket on StubHub, you won't be allowed to come into this show.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要确保，如果你是在 StubHub 上买的票，你将不被允许进入这场演出。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Like they couldn't come into the concert?
sentences.zh: 就像他们不能去听音乐会一样？

sentences.en: Well, and ultimately, the complaint says that StubHub had to work with Ticketmaster to fulfill the tickets that had already been sold, that they stopped selling new tickets, and
sentences.zh: 嗯，最终，起诉书称 StubHub 不得不与 Ticketmaster 合作来兑现已经售出的门票，他们停止出售新门票，

sentences.en: that hundreds of people who bought their tickets on StubHub didn't get into the show.
sentences.zh: 并且数百名在 StubHub 上买票的人最终没能进场观看演出。

sentences.en: That seems very unfair.
sentences.zh: 这看起来太不公平了。

sentences.en: Like they bought a ticket.
sentences.zh: 就像他们明明买过票一样。

sentences.en: Well, and according to the Justice Department, it didn't stop there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，据司法部称，事情并没有就此结束。

sentences.en: That Live Nation used its industry connections to pressure an investor in TEG, this company
sentences.zh: Live Nation 利用其行业人脉向 TEG 的一位投资者施压，而 TEG 正是被其视为威胁的公司，

sentences.en: that it viewed as a threat, and that it pushed that investor to pull back from its relationship with TEG, which obviously would have weakened this potential competitor.
sentences.zh: 它敦促该投资者切断与 TEG 的关系，这显然会削弱这个潜在的竞争对手。

sentences.en: So these are very strong armed tactics.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是非常强硬的手段。

sentences.en: What is the DOJ saying is the result of all of this?
sentences.zh: 司法部认为这一切的结果是什么？

sentences.en: Like what does all of this amount to?
sentences.zh: 所有这一切究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: It says that all of this adds up to higher fees for consumers and a worse product, a worse quality ticketing experience when fans go to buy, because Live Nation doesn't have to
sentences.zh: 它表示，这一切最终导致消费者支付更高的费用，产品质量更差，当歌迷去买票时体验更糟，因为 Live Nation 根本无需与任何人竞争。

sentences.en: compete with anyone.
sentences.zh: 它不需要为了应对竞争对手而进行创新。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to innovate in response to competitors.
sentences.zh: 它不需要为了应对竞争对手而进行创新。

sentences.en: So among other things, the Justice Department wants to break this company up, at the very least
sentences.zh: 因此，在诸多诉求中，司法部希望拆分这家公司，至少要将 Ticketmaster（票务部门、售票处部门）与

sentences.en: by separating Ticketmaster, the ticketing unit, the box office unit, from the rest of Live
sentences.zh: Live Nation 的其余部分（负责所有其他业务，如推广演唱会、拥有场馆等）剥离开来。

sentences.en: Nation that does all these other things, promotes concerts, owns venues, et cetera.
sentences.zh: Live Nation 的其余部分（负责所有其他业务，如推广演唱会、拥有场馆等）剥离开来。

sentences.en: So in other words, go back to the way it was in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，回到最初的状态。

sentences.en: Yeah, or as much as you can.
sentences.zh: 是的，或者说尽可能地回到过去。

sentences.en: And why does that fix the problem?
sentences.zh: 为什么这样就能解决问题呢？

sentences.en: Well, the Justice Department doesn't say a lot on this point, but it's clear that what they want to do with this lawsuit is disrupt this cycle where Live Nation's power reinforces
sentences.zh: 嗯，司法部在这点上没有说太多，但很明显，他们希望通过这起诉讼打破这样一个循环：Live Nation 的权力不断自我强化，一次又一次，没完没了。

sentences.en: itself again and again and again.
sentences.zh: Live Nation 的权力不断自我强化，一次又一次，没完没了。

sentences.en: And what does Live Nation say in response?
sentences.zh: 对此 Live Nation 是怎么回应的？

sentences.en: I imagine they disagree with all of this.
sentences.zh: 我猜他们不同意这一切。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实不同意。

sentences.en: They've said a lot.
sentences.zh: 他们说了很多。

sentences.en: And they start out by saying something that will be familiar to you because other companies that have been accused of antitrust violations.
sentences.zh: 他们首先说了一些你会感到熟悉的话，因为其他被指控违反反垄断法的公司

sentences.en: They say it as well, which is that they don't fit the profile of a monopoly.
sentences.zh: 也说过同样的话，那就是他们不符合垄断企业的特征。

sentences.en: That their overall profit margins are lower than those of companies like Meta or Apple or Google.
sentences.zh: 他们的整体利润率低于 Meta、苹果或谷歌等公司。

sentences.en: And that even if you look at Ticketmaster specifically, they take a smaller percentage of every sale than a lot of other digital platforMs.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使你专门看看 Ticketmaster，他们从每笔交易中抽取的比例也比许多其他数字平台要低。

sentences.en: So they say basically the numbers show that we don't have the kind of power you would normally associate with a monopoly.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是在说，数字表明我们并不具备你通常与垄断联系在一起的那种权力。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And then they say, listen, we know that there are things that fans don't like about the ticketing experience.
sentences.zh: 然后他们说，听着，我们知道歌迷对购票体验有不满意的地方。

sentences.en: There may be fixes to those, but largely it's not Live Nation's fault, they say.
sentences.zh: 这些问题也许有解决的办法，但他们说，这在很大程度上并不是 Live Nation 的错。

sentences.en: They say that artists generally set the prices they want people to pay for tickets.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，通常是艺术家自己设定了他们希望人们为门票支付的价格。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: So artists themselves do it.
sentences.zh: 所以是艺术家自己决定的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That artists sign off on how much a ticket will cost to their shows.
sentences.zh: 艺术家亲笔签署了他们演出的门票价格。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And they also say that demand sometimes drives ticket prices up.
sentences.zh: 他们还表示，需求有时会推高票价。

sentences.en: If there are more people who want to see a show than there are seats or standing room to see that show, the prices will be higher.
sentences.zh: 如果有更多的人想要看演出，而看演出的座位或站席有限，价格就会上涨。

sentences.en: And finally, they say that there's this kind of pernicious outside force of scalpers, people who resell tickets that use bots to hoover up way more tickets than they could possibly
sentences.zh: 最后，他们表示，存在一种有害的外部力量，那就是黄牛——那些使用机器人抢购远远超出他们可能使用的门票、

sentences.en: use and then resell them at a higher price.
sentences.zh: 然后以更高价格转售票的人。

sentences.en: And so they say that all of these things may contribute to a fan experience that people don't like, but that it's not necessarily Live Nation's fault.
sentences.zh: 因此他们认为，所有这些因素可能会导致歌迷体验不佳，但这并不一定是 Live Nation 的错。

sentences.en: I mean, to me, this makes certain sense.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对我来说，这在某种程度上是讲得通的。

sentences.en: I guess if you think of, you know, a Taylor Swift show and lots of people trying to buy
sentences.zh: 我想如果你想到，比如说，泰勒·斯威夫特的演唱会和许多人争相买票的情景，

sentences.en: tickets, you know, one reason why those tickets are expensive is not necessarily because there's
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些票之所以昂贵的一个原因，不一定是因为有什么不可告人的勾当，

sentences.en: something nefarious going on, but because lots of people want to buy tickets and there's a market and, you know, supply and demand has a role here.
sentences.zh: 而是因为很多人都想买票，这是一个市场，而且你知道的，供求关系在这里发挥了作用。

sentences.en: Well, and a clear question here that I have that other people have asked is, how much does
sentences.zh: 嗯，我以及其他人问过的一个显而易见的问题是，司法部认为因为所谓的 Live Nation 垄断，票价到底上涨了多少？

sentences.en: the Justice Department think ticket prices have gone up because of this alleged Live Nation monopoly?
sentences.zh: 司法部并没有回答这个问题。

sentences.en: And the Justice Department hasn't answered that question.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把它与周围的所有其他因素、市场力量以及其他一切剥离开来。

sentences.en: They haven't disentangled it with all of the other stuff that's around, market forces, everything.
sentences.zh: 他们没有把它与周围的所有其他因素、市场力量以及其他一切剥离开来。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没。错。

sentences.en: And there's another element of Live Nation's response that we should mention, which is that
sentences.zh: Live Nation 的回应中还有另一个我们应该提及的要素，那就是该公司基本上声称这场诉讼是有政治动机的，

sentences.en: the company basically says this lawsuit is politically motivated, that this administration,
sentences.zh: 现任政府——拜登政府——正在提起一些站不住脚、反商业的诉讼。

sentences.en: the Biden administration, is bringing lawsuits that don't hold a lot of water, but are anti-business.
sentences.zh: 现任政府——拜登政府——正在提起一些站不住脚、反商业的诉讼。

sentences.en: That's what Live Nation is saying.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Live Nation 的说法。

sentences.en: I mean, it does sort of ring true in some sense, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种意义上说，这确实听起来有几分道理，对吧？

sentences.en: This has been the tilt of this administration toward cracking down on big companies.
sentences.zh: 现任政府一直以来的倾向就是严厉打击大公司。

sentences.en: The DOJ has changed in this respect.
sentences.zh: 司法部在这方面已经发生了变化。

sentences.en: They're filing a lawsuit to break up a merger that a previous DOJ had actually approved.
sentences.zh: 他们正在提起诉讼，以拆分一个此前司法部实际上已经批准过的并购案。

sentences.en: Well, you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得对。

sentences.en: This Department of Justice, this administration more broadly, has a different view about antitruSt.
sentences.zh: 这个司法部，以及更广泛的现任政府，对反垄断有着不同的看法。

sentences.en: They think that antitrust law can be a more expansive tool to address problems in the economy.
sentences.zh: 他们认为反垄断法可以成为解决经济问题的更广阔的工具。

sentences.en: And they've put that into practice.
sentences.zh: 他们已经将这一点付诸实践。

sentences.en: They've sued Google for violating anti-monopoly laws.
sentences.zh: 他们起诉谷歌违反反垄断法。

sentences.en: They've sued Apple for violating anti-monopoly laws.
sentences.zh: 他们起诉苹果违反反垄断法。

sentences.en: But I think ultimately what they believe is that they're responding to a change in the economy, that these companies have gotten much bigger, that they have gotten more powerful,
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们最终的信念是，他们是在应对经济的变化，这些公司已经变得庞大得多，权力大得多，

sentences.en: and they are responding to the way the companies broke the law on their way to becoming that big.
sentences.zh: 而他们正在针对这些公司在发展壮大过程中触犯法律的行为做出回应。

sentences.en: So, David, when you and I talked about Google and Apple, you referenced them here, you know, we talked about how there were broad repercussions for the future on American society.
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，当我和你谈论谷歌和苹果时，你在这里提到了它们，你知道的，我们讨论了这会对美国社会的未来产生广泛的影响。

sentences.en: What would you say the implications are in this case?
sentences.zh: 你认为本案的含义是什么？

sentences.en: This case, ultimately, for the Justice Department, is about the market for culture and creativity.
sentences.zh: 对司法部而言，这个案件最终关乎文化与创意的市场。

sentences.en: You know, a few years ago, the Justice Department successfully blocked Penguin Random House, a big publisher, from buying Simon & Schuster, another publisher.
sentences.zh: 你知道，几年前，司法部成功阻止了大型出版商企鹅兰登书屋收购另一家出版商西蒙与舒斯特。

sentences.en: And they said that one problem with this merger was that it would reduce how much authors got paid,
sentences.zh: 他们表示，这场并购的一个问题在于，它会减少作者的稿酬，

sentences.en: and that it would create a market where fewer books and fewer types of stories broke through.
sentences.zh: 并且会创造这样一个市场：更少的书籍和更少类型的故事能够脱颖而出。

sentences.en: This Justice Department is embracing an idea that the more concentrated the economy gets,
sentences.zh: 本届司法部正在拥抱这样一种观点：经济集中度越高，

sentences.en: the more it stifles creative expression, the ability of artists to make art and get it to the public, and the ability of the public to consume it.
sentences.zh: 就越会扼杀创意表达、艺术家创作艺术并将其推向公众的能力，以及公众消费它的能力。

sentences.en: And that, they say, is a central question of democracy.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这是民主的核心问题。

sentences.en: Because things like music are how we talk about big social issues or big political issues.
sentences.zh: 因为诸如音乐之类的事物正是我们讨论重大社会议题或重大政治议题的方式。

sentences.en: So that is, they say, what's at the heart of this case, that it is not just about the fees, it's not just about how much an artist gets paid,
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，这才是本案的核心所在——它不仅关乎费用，不仅关乎艺术家能拿到多少报酬，

sentences.en: but it's about whether or not there is a fair marketplace for ideas, and whether or not consumers are able to access it.
sentences.zh: 但这关乎思想市场上是否存在公平竞争，以及消费者能否接触到这些思想。

sentences.en: David, thank you.
sentences.zh: 大卫，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito declined to recuse himself from two cases arising from the January 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol,
sentences.zh: 周三，最高法院大法官塞缪尔·阿利托拒绝在两起涉及2021年1月6日国会山袭击事件的案件中回避，

sentences.en: after The Times reported that flags displayed outside his houses appeared to support the Stop the Steal movement.
sentences.zh: 此前《纽约时报》报道称，他住所外悬挂的旗帜似乎支持“阻止窃选”运动。

sentences.en: In letters to Democratic members of Congress who had demanded his recusal,
sentences.zh: 在致要求他回避的民主党国会议员的信中，

sentences.en: Justice Alito said that the flags at his home in Virginia and a beach house in New Jersey were flown by his wife, Martha Ann, and that he had had nothing to do with it.
sentences.zh: 阿利托大法官表示，他位于弗吉尼亚州的家和新泽西州的海滨度假屋的旗帜是由他的妻子玛莎·安悬挂的，他对此毫无干涉。

sentences.en: And a group of 12 New York jurors deliberated for more than four hours in the final stretch of the criminal trial of Donald Trump,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，在唐纳德·特朗普刑事审判的最后阶段，12名纽约陪审团成员商议了四个多小时，

sentences.en: in which the former president is accused of falsifying business records.
sentences.zh: 这位前总统被指控伪造商业记录。

sentences.en: The jurors asked for portions of the testimony from two witnesses to be read back to them, as well as the judge's instructions.
sentences.zh: 陪审团要求重读两名证人的部分证词以及法官的指示。

sentences.en: They were then dismissed for the day and will resume deliberations today.
sentences.zh: 随后他们结束了当天的庭审，并将在今天恢复商议。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Will Reed, Rob Zipko, and Michelle Bongia.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由威尔·里德、罗布·齐普科和米歇尔·邦吉亚制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Michael Benoit and Brendan Klinkenberg.
sentences.zh: 节目由迈克尔·贝努瓦和布伦丹·克林肯伯格剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marian Lozano, Dan Powell, and Will Reed.
sentences.zh: 包含马里安·洛萨诺、丹·鲍威尔和威尔·里德的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 音频工程由阿丽莎·莫克斯利负责。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德利的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔维内西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了许多自称是改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
